Subject: Astranova dedicated inference footprint — data & traces request

Hi Samir / Elena,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. To put together a clear committed-reserved plan and an accurate GPU-fleet estimate for Astranova, we need a concise view of your current and expected inference profile. I've attached a quick form but below are the high-value items that drive sizing decisions — if you can provide approximate numbers for each, that will let us model cost and latency tradeoffs quickly: 

- Traffic shape: typical RPS and peak RPS (15-min peak vs sustained) and expected % growth next 6 months.
- Concurrent sessions: average and peak concurrent sessions (if applicable).
- Prompt / response token distribution: median prompt length, 90th pct response length, and % of queries that stream.
- Session duration & KV cache hit-rate: typical session lifetimes (secs/mins) and whether you expect key-value reuse across messages.
- E2E latency targets: p50/p95/p99 targets for interactive flows and background/batch flows.
- Workload mix: % of classification/embedding vs generation vs chat and any heavy multi-turn agents.
- Model family & quantization tolerance: which model(s) you plan to run (open LLM names) and whether 8-bit/4-bit quantization is acceptable.
- Data retention / security notes: any constraints that would force Private/VPC deployment.

Attachment: dedicated_sizing_form_v2.xlsx (a short table you can fill) — if you prefer, paste answers inline.

If you can send sample request traces or a token histogram (CSV) that captures a few days of representative traffic, that would be the most helpful input for sizing. We can run a short sizing-pass and get back with a preliminary GPU-slab and cost range the same day.

Proposed next step: 30-min sizing workshop where we walk a short sample through our estimator. Are you available this week for a quick call? 

Appreciate it,
Karthik
Head of Presales, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Astranova dedicated inference footprint — data & traces request

Karthik — thanks, this is helpful. I filled out the high-level bits below and attached a token histogram export. Quick answers:

- Typical RPS: 25 req/s average, peak 420 req/s (10–15 min bursts during product refreshes). Expect ~20% QoQ growth.
- Concurrency: avg sessions ~180, peak concurrent sessions ~2,100 during bursts.
- Tokens: median prompt 42 tokens, median response 110 tokens, 90th pct response ~420 tokens. Around 22% of requests use streaming for long responses.
- Sessions & KV: session lifespan ~4–6 minutes for our chat flows; KV cache hit-rate estimate ~65% for multi-turn agents.
- Latency targets: interactive p50 ~120ms, p95 < 420ms, p99 < 900ms (hard business requirement during checkout flows). Background/batch not latency sensitive.
- Workload mix: 70% chat generation, 20% embedding/classification, 10% background batch jobs.
- Model family: plan to use an LlamaX-13B variant initially; we'd like to evaluate 8-bit first and consider 4-bit after validation.
- Security: must be Private/VPC for PCI-related data; SOC2 in progress.

Attachment: astranova_token_histogram.csv (sample 72-hour export).

We can do the workshop on Thursday afternoon PST. Let me know a 30-minute slot and we’ll confirm.

—Samir
Head of Platform, Astranova

Thanks Samir — this is excellent. Two quick clarifying asks so our sizing pass has the right knobs: 

1) Burst shape: can you confirm whether the 420 req/s peak is mostly sustained for the whole 10–15 minute window or if there are micro-bursts inside (e.g., multiple 30–60s spikes stacked inside the 15m window)? We ask because micro-bursts change the effective batching and GPU utilization assumptions.

2) Model latency envelope: do you have a rough per-token generation speed (tokens/sec) observed for the LlamaX-13B on your current infra, or alternatively the average tokens generated per request for the 70% chat mix when you see 110 tokens median? That helps map model compute to expected GPU slots.

Suggested mapping and quick estimate notes (preliminary):
- If the 420 req/s peak is sustained across 15m and most responses are ~110 tokens, we’ll likely size for a mix of on-demand GPU slabs and a reserved pool sized to handle the 95th pct sustained throughput.
- With 65% KV hit-rate, effective compute per request reduces — we’ll simulate both 60% and 80% hit scenarios.

I attached a short cheatsheet that shows the inputs we use for our estimator and a candidate workshop agenda.

Attachment: redwood-dedicated-sizing-cheatsheet.pdf (1-page).

Proposal: Thu 16 Sep 2026, 16:00–16:30 PST for a workshop with Karthik + Marissa + a systems engineer from our side. Does that work?

Thanks,
Priyom
Presales Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Priyom / Karthik — thanks for the notes. Confirming the workshop time works for us. Quick answers to your clarifying Qs: 

- Burst shape: the 420 req/s peaks are typically a bit spiky — we usually see 2–3 micro-peaks inside the 10–15m window where traffic briefly jumps 20–30% above the nominal peak for 30–90s.
- Per-token speed: we ran LlamaX-13B on a local A100 dev box and see ~1,100 tokens/sec throughput in our tests; avg tokens generated per chat request is about 115 when considering multi-turn.

Forwarding Samir's CSV export as a quick reference — we aim to bring a 3-day telemetry slice during the workshop.

Onward — see you Thu 16:00 PST.

Best,
